step1_analysis.description: A digitally controlled delay line consisting of a current-starved inverter followed by a three-stage standard inverter buffer chain. The delay is monotonically adjusted by switching PMOS transistors in a diode-connected bias network, which modulates the control voltage (VG) and the tail current of the first stage.

paper_reference.title: A Monotonic Digitally Controlled Delay Element

delay_min.description: Minimum propagation delay from IN to OUT (when control input A=0, maximizing bias voltage and tail current).

sky130_expected.calculation: With a 2pF load, the output stage delay dominates. dt = C*dV/I = 2pF*0.9V/2.5mA = 720ps. Combined with the intrinsic delay of 4 stages, total delay is ~1-2ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Matches the order of magnitude of the paper's 2.06ns reported value, assuming the 2pF load is applied.

delay_max.description: Maximum propagation delay from IN to OUT (when control input A=1.8V, reducing bias voltage and tail current).

sky130_expected.calculation: Delay increases as tail current decreases when A=1.8V turns off one of the pull-up PMOS devices in the bias network.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Expected to be higher than delay_min, aligning with the 2.42ns reported value.

delay_resolution.description: Difference in delay between adjacent digital control states (A=0 vs A=1.8V).

sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports 2ps resolution for a full multi-bit vector. With only one effective bit toggling a large W=5u transistor in this extracted netlist, the step size will be larger.

power_consumption.description: Average static and dynamic power consumption during operation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Static power from bias network (~400uA * 1.8V = 720uW) + Dynamic power (2pF * 1.8V^2 * 50MHz = 324uW).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Higher than paper due to the unoptimized W=5u L=0.5u sizing in the extracted netlist and the heavy 2pF load.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure minimum delay, maximum delay, and average power consumption by toggling the digital control input A halfway through the simulation.
